one_line_contribution: A matched-volume decoupling experiment claiming that diversity collapse in self-editing agent memory is caused by growing the bank from retrieval-conditioned episodes (the collection policy) rather than by the quality of what is written, plus a 2x2 crossing with a reflective prompt optimizer and an instruction/bank transplant showing the evolved instruction itself absorbs and carries the contraction.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, in different directions. (a) CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739) states the identical structural premise — retrieval determines usage signals, updated bank reshapes retrieval — so the mechanism is already named in print; what remains for this proposal is the sign of the effect and one ablation (a memory-off collection arm), which is a standard control rather than a new idea. The proposal concedes this and it is a fair concession, but the honesty does not restore the novelty. (b) ExpeL-lineage practice is the underrated threat: ExpeL extracts insights from a separately collected training pool, i.e. collection episodes that are not conditioned on the bank being built. Arm A2 is therefore close to earlier standard practice, and M50 (50% memory-off collection) is the fresh-data mixing-ratio knob already established in the model-collapse literature the proposal cites (Shumailov et al.; LLM Web Dynamics). So the diagnostic framing may be new; the proposed intervention is a rediscovery of an older design plus a known knob.
strongest_objection: The primary contrast, A1 vs A2, cannot arbitrate the proposal's own dichotomy (collection policy vs content), because memory-off collecting episodes produce different trajectories and therefore different written items — content is not held fixed, it is exactly what varies. Every content-side account in the related work predicts prediction 3 (A2 tail exceeds A1 tail by >=6 points) with no appeal to retrieval self-reinforcement: OEP's locally-correct-but-non-transferable experiences and Trap of Trajectory's spurious feature-outcome correlations are both *more* likely in memory-conditioned episodes. B2 is offered as the discriminator, but it gates verification plus self-consistency, i.e. hallucination and inconsistency only; it does not gate spuriousness or non-transferability. So prediction 4's 'B2 tracks A1, not A2' would refute one narrow content account while the abstract and title claim it refutes the content account in general. Second, the write composition is matched only in count. Sampling W=40 successful episodes uniformly means A1 — which by the proposal's own head/tail story succeeds disproportionately on the five large head clusters — writes head-skewed items simply because of where it succeeded. Prediction 2's >=25% cluster-coverage drop and much of the effective-rank decline in prediction 1 then follow mechanically from differential success location, not from preferential attachment in retrieval. The plan never reports, let alone matches, the per-cluster composition of the 40 written items per arm. Third, the compounding half of the title is pre-declared possibly unresolvable: the 2x2 interaction MDE is 8-10 points against a prediction stated at 8, so prong 2 is powered to return 'underpowered' and the transplant test is left carrying it.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a write-blinded coupled arm: collecting episodes read memory as in A1, but distillation runs on the trajectory with retrieved items masked out. This is the arm that separates 'memory changed the trajectory' from 'memory contaminated the distillation', which is the actual content/policy split being claimed. (2) Cluster-stratify the write sampling so the per-cluster composition of each cycle's 40 items is matched across A1 and A2, and report per-arm write composition as a first-class table; without it, predictions 1 and 2 are confounded with success location. (3) Add a content-transplant arm — grow a bank from A1's items subsampled to A2's effective rank, and the converse — so the mechanism claim is tested with provenance held fixed; the existing shuffled-provenance placebo only relabels text and does not do this. (4) Establish a null band for the transplant contrast with a within-arm instruction swap (A4 instruction from seed i evaluated on A4 bank from seed j). Prediction 7's 4-point threshold compares instructions produced by two different GEPA runs at 6 candidates per cycle; 4 points is plausibly inside optimizer-seed variance, and nothing in the design bounds that. (5) Actually test preferential attachment — fit retrieval-count growth against current count across cycles — instead of asserting 'rich get richer' and measuring only Gini and effective rank, neither of which distinguishes a self-reinforcing process from a one-shot compositional skew. (6) Broaden B2 to include a non-transferability/spuriousness gate, or stop claiming the content account is refuted.
missing_baseline: A reduced deployment-time injection-budget arm. The track's established prior result is that cutting injection from seven retrieved items to three eliminated the harm from the *same* bank — volume, not content, was the measured lever. This plan freezes k=4 in every arm at every evaluation and never varies it, so a coupled bank evaluated at k=1-2 is absent. If that cell removes A1's tail deficit, the correct recommendation is 'inject less at read time' at zero collection cost, which dominates M50 and decoupled collection entirely, and the paper's headline fix is beaten by the track's own earlier finding. B1 varies *which* items are injected under coupling, not how many, so it does not cover this. A secondary omission: no arm decouples the optimizer's evaluation episodes from the bank while leaving the bank coupled at deployment, so the 2x2 confounds 'optimizer saw contracted retrievals' with 'optimizer's episodes also fed the bank'.
preprint_collision: The check is above average for this track and should be credited: it names CoEvo-Mem (2608.01739) as an essentially identical mechanistic premise, refuses to minimize it, states plainly that a reviewer may read prong 1 as an adversarial test of someone else's premise, and pre-commits to what happens if CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready contains a decoupled-collection ablation. That is the right posture. It is nonetheless incomplete in three ways. It reports conclusions but no search record — no queries, date range, or venues — so its coverage cannot be judged, and it concedes no OpenReview 2026 sweep. It does not search for the one thing that decides prong 1's novelty: whether offline / memory-off experience collection already exists as a compared condition in the ExpeL and ReasoningBank lineage, where separating a collection phase from a deployment phase is closer to standard practice than to a novel control. And it does not look for the self-consuming-RAG / synthetic-corpus-loop preprint cluster beyond 2602.16136, which is where a matched-volume decoupled-corpus experiment would most plausibly already sit. Verdict on the check: honest and specific, but it establishes that the mechanism is already claimed in print and leaves novelty resting on an ablation whose absence from the literature has not actually been demonstrated.
